title: Ācamana: the three names

words.meaning: to Acyuta, ‘the one who does not fall’

words.gram: n. nom. sg., indecl. in use

translation.literal: To Acyuta, salutation. To Ananta, salutation. To Govinda, salutation.
translation.readable: Salutation to Acyuta, to Ananta, to Govinda.

meaning: Three names of Viṣṇu, each with namaḥ, ‘salutation’, said as water is sipped from the right palm three times. The ācamana purifies the performer before the rite and is repeated at its joints. Acyuta is ‘the one who does not fall away’, Ananta ‘the endless’, and Govinda a name of Kṛṣṇa as the finder or keeper of cows.
in_the_rite: The opening ācamana (step acamana): water is sipped once with each name; the face and body are then touched with the twelve names (anga-vandana).

notes.label: direct
notes.text: namaḥ with the dative is the ordinary formula of salutation: ‘to X, bowing’.
